subject: Packaging tradeoffs: anchor commitment vs burst credits — Skyline pilot
messages:
From: Oliver Shaw <oliver@skyline.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot packaging question — anchor vs burst credits

David —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our execs want to move the pilot forward but procurement is flagging the platform fee and the operator-license path. Two quick questions so we can evaluate: 1) If we take a small anchor commitment (3 months) can we get a larger migration safeguard (exit credit) in lieu of a longer-term amortized platform fee? 2) Alternatively, if we keep the platform fee minimal, can we buy burst credits to cover anticipated initial ramp spikes (and how do those credits price vs committed nodes)?

We need a simple TCO sketch we can show to CFO by EOD Friday. Any chance you can propose two short options (anchor commitment + exit safeguard vs low platform fee + burst credits) with SRE support tiers mapped?

Appreciate it —
Oliver
Oliver Shaw
VP Product, Skyline AI
--
Attachment: Skyline_Pilot_Specs.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging question — anchor vs burst credits

Oliver —

Thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Marissa (commercial) and Naomi (finance) to sketch two concrete options and a short ops/SLA mapping. We can do:

Option A — Anchor commitment (3 months, small node commit): 10% reduced per-node rate, exit safeguard = prorated migration credit equal to 40% of remaining platform fee for first 6 months. Includes Standard SRE (business hours) and 4hr response for severity 1.

Option B — Low platform fee + burst credits: platform fee reduced ~60% vs our standard starter. Burst credits priced at $0.60/token-equivalent (example) with a guaranteed holdback of 2x monthly burst spend as a refundable deposit; includes Premium SRE during pilot (24/7 on-call for sev1) as a paid add-on.

We'll attach an ops breakdown and a terse term sheet for you to share. Naomi — can you confirm the finance wording and whether we can be firm on the 40% migration credit for Option A?

-David
David Kim
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot packaging question — pilot options and cost sketch

Oliver, David —

Drafting concise TCO excerpts below (numbers are illustrative; final terms in attached term sheet):

Option A — Anchor (3mo commit)
- Commit: 3 months, 4 dedicated operator nodes (reserved)
- Discount: 10% off per-node compute + waived onboarding fee
- Platform fee treatment: full platform fee amortized monthly; if customer elects to exit within first 6 months, they receive a migration safeguard credit equal to 40% of remaining platform fee (applied toward tooling/exit assistance).
- Support: Standard SRE (Mon–Fri business hours) + 24/7 escalation dial-in for sev1 for first 60 days
- Pros: predictable unit economics; cheaper per-token base; easier capacity planning
- Cons: higher upfront plate for customers worried about adoption risk

Option B — Low platform fee + burst credits
- Commit: month-to-month pilot, no reserved nodes; burst credits purchased upfront for pilot (50k credit units)
- Pricing: platform fee reduced by ~60% for pilot period; burst credits priced at a premium vs reserved capacity (example: 65% of per-token reserved price)
- Deposit: refundable deposit equivalent to 2x expected monthly burst usage; refunded at pilot close less any overage
- Support: Premium SRE (on-call, 24/7) included for the pilot duration
- Pros: low capital lock; easy to scale bursts; lower perceived risk by procurement
- Cons: higher marginal cost for sustained usage; possible throttling if credits deplete

Attached: concise term sheet and ops_breakdown.xlsx showing node vs burst delta. David — if this looks good I can bake into a short term sheet and a tidy DocuSign for Oliver.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ops_breakdown.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging question — finance notes on migration credit

Oliver / team —

Finance confirms we can commit to the 40% migration safeguard credit for Option A under these constraints: (a) commitment must be explicitly 3 months minimum, (b) migration credit only applies to the platform fee portion and not to consumed compute or third-party licenses, (c) credit claim must be made within 90 days of contract termination and applied to professional services / tiered exit support invoices.

For Option B (burst credits), deposit handling: we require the 2x refundable deposit be held as a customer hold on our billing; any unused burst funds will be returned within 45 days of pilot close, minus any reconciliation items. We can provide a short amortization schedule and cash flow impact statement if Skyline's CFO wants it.

-Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Finance Lead, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
